findings.summary: The new check `[[ $comp == "$cur"* ]]` passes when both $comp and $cur are empty, so a line with an empty value (e.g. `\tsome description`) is added to COMPREPLY as a blank candidate; the old compgen-based code filtered these out.

The no-description path (line 183) uses `compgen -W "$out"`, which splits on whitespace and expands `$` and backticks, while the description path (line 194) does a literal prefix match, so the same completion behaves differently depending on whether any line has a description.
